clue.text: Plant destruction by insect

explanation.definitionFit: Bugloss is a bristly flowering herb of the borage family, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Permit loan to be set up? I don't know

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised and so reads from the bottom

a quiz contestant says pass when they cannot answer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to arrange a loan, unsure of the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: A bus pass is a British concession card giving free or cheap bus travel, usually to pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus pass is a travel permit, a document authorising its holder to ride buses.

clue.text: Actress mainly crows over Oscar

explanation.surface: A star boasts endlessly about her Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar suggests the film award, fitting the actress, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a celebrated Swedish-born Hollywood film star of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Totalitarian state briefly incorrect about charging a new criminal

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Drives away mules, perhaps in pick-up

clue.text: PM I see suppressing nonsense

explanation.walkthrough: Squit is an East Anglian word for nonsense, so the dialect may be new to many solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith was the Liberal Prime Minister of Britain from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Unexpectedly scans one with a sound resemblance?

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Subdue, in the capacity of mum

explanation.surface: A mother is asked to keep children in order.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum looks like mother; it is the adjective for silent, as in keep mum.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash a rebellion is to suppress or crush it.

clue.text: I relish digesting volume one on your American and Russian news

explanation.definitionFit: Izvestiya was the official Soviet government daily; its name is Russian for news.

clue.text: Papacy's unknown saint beginning to engage in breach

explanation.walkthrough: The 's means is: Papacy is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the jurisdiction of the Pope, the papal authority itself.

clue.text: Gang in bars — might they check consumption of coke?

definitions.text: might they check consumption of coke?

indicators.note: the gang word is placed in the middle of the word for bars

parts.note: stops is a verb meaning bars or prevents
a crew is a gang of workers or companions

explanation.surface: A gang of drinkers in pubs wonders whether anything will stop them drinking cola.
explanation.walkthrough: Bars suggests pubs, but it is the verb meaning prevents; coke is the soft drink, kept fizzy by the cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw-on lids seal bottles of cola, so they control when the drink can be consumed.

clue.text: Article, verb and pronoun finish off grammatical block

explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block on which a smith hammers metal.

clue.text: Shell ban by Israel, seething

explanation.walkthrough: Shell looks like the oil company, but it is a verb telling you to remove the outside of the ban word.

clue.text: Building up NHS? Yes, it's struggling

clue.text: Current in fuse applied to keep going

parts.note: solder is to fuse metal pieces together

on, as in a plaster put on a cut

explanation.walkthrough: The electrical words (current, fuse) set the scene, but fuse here is the verb meaning join metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is an idiom for persisting doggedly in spite of difficulty.

clue.text: Drink in casual milieu with Jack inside church

CE is the Church of England

explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters with the J inside them are then followed by CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime juice is the juice of limes, drunk as a cordial, so it is a beverage.

clue.text: Strikes again disrupted teachers around 3rd of December

explanation.walkthrough: Strikes suggests industrial action by the teachers; here it is catches again, as fish strike a bait.
explanation.definitionFit: Recatches means catches once more, and to strike is to hook a fish, so the sense is seize again.

clue.text: Bag English beef

clue.text: Perhaps fixes Head of Intelligence in thought, affording protection in trap

clue.text: Vote in a fellow King, maybe

explanation.definitionFit: Blues star B. B. King was a celebrated guitar player, an example of an axman in musicians' slang.

clue.text: In draughts, maybe peg's secured bloomers?

clue.text: Thrash about, needing energy food

clue.text: Everlasting bearing evenly coated in lead-free alloy
